content: Before starting rabeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently using. This is important to avoid potential interactions. Refer to the Interactions section for further details. Do not take rabeprazole unless it has been prescribed specifically for you by a healthcare provider. Always follow the prescribed dosage and instructions. Do not share rabeprazole with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may cause harm. Keep rabeprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the tablets. If needed, antacids can be taken alongside rabeprazole. However, rabeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn, as it may take 1 to 4 days to achieve its full effect. Before using rabeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about your complete medical history, including any current or past health conditions. Specifically, let them know if you have low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), or liver problems. This information will help your provider determine if rabeprazole is appropriate for you. Rabeprazole may interact with other medications and supplements. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and OTC medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Pay special attention to medications such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, and certain antiretroviral drugs like rilpivirine, nelfinavir, or saquinavir. Rabeprazole may also affect the absorption of some medications. Always provide a complete list of your medications to your healthcare provider. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known whether rabeprazole can harm an unborn baby. Your provider will advise you on whether you should take rabeprazole during pregnancy. Similarly, it is unknown if rabeprazole passes into breast milk, so consult your provider if you are breastfeeding. Rabeprazole can generally be taken with or without food. However, if you are using it to treat duodenal ulcers or Helicobacter pylori infections, take it after a meal. The effects of alcohol on rabeprazole are not well understood, so consult your provider if you have concerns. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much rabeprazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double or extra doses. Rabeprazole is used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Rabeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Rabeprazole is available as 20 mg delayed-release oral tablets under the brand name AcipHex and as generic rabeprazole. Store rabeprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. Common side effects of rabeprazole include pain, sore throat, gas, infections, constipation, headache (in children aged 12 to 17), diarrhea (in children aged 12 to 17), nausea, vomiting, and stomach pain (in children aged 12 to 17). If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here. Contact your provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. Serious side effects of rabeprazole include kidney problems, such as acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, which can occur at any time during treatment. Symptoms include decreased urine output or blood in the urine. Seek medical attention immediately if these occur. Rabeprazole may cause antibiotic-associated diarrhea due to an overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your provider immediately if you experience these symptoms. Severe skin reactions, such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), can occur and may be life-threatening. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes, blisters on the skin or mucous membranes, and red, watery eyes. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms develop. Rabeprazole can cause a severe allergic reaction called Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), which may affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop taking rabeprazole and seek immediate medical attention if these occur. Rabeprazole may trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Inform your provider if these symptoms develop. Long-term use of rabeprazole (three years or more) may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency, as it reduces vitamin absorption. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling in the hands or feet. Contact your provider if you experience these symptoms. Rabeprazole can cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which may lead to seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. People taking rabeprazole long-term or with other medications that lower magnesium levels are at higher risk. Stop taking rabeprazole and contact your provider if these symptoms occur. Rabeprazole may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults or those taking high doses or using it long-term. Discuss this risk with your provider if you have concerns. Rabeprazole may cause serious allergic reactions. Symptoms include difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, facial swelling, trouble swallowing, itching, rash, or hives. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms occur. Do not use rabeprazole if you are allergic to it, any proton pump inhibitor, or any of its ingredients. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients in the specific rabeprazole product you are using. Rabeprazole should not be taken with certain other medications. Always inform your provider about all medications and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions.
